text: Shri Krishna says that devotion does
not mean sitting for hours with folded
hands. Devotion is when you feed a
hungry person and move on without
seeking recognition. When you sit
quietly beside someone who is weeping.
When you see someone’s mistake but do
not embarrass them in front of others.
One who searches for God in temples but
cannot see Him in humans, their search
is incomplete. Worship of the mind is
the highest form of worship. Flowers,
lamps, and offerings are all external
means. But the true offering is a pure
mind that holds no bitterness for
anyone. The Lord does not look at the
value of your offerings. He looks at
your intentions. Before a single true
tear, a thousand performative prayers
pale in comparison. Even when
everything is going well in life,
remember the one who brought you this
far. Often, a person forgets in
happiness and calls out only in sorrow.
But for one who thanks Him even in
happiness, sorrows become lighter
before they even arrive. Gratitude is
the medicine that requires no
prescription. In the end, just
understand that life is not a book you
can rewrite. Every day is a new page,
and the pen is in your hand. If you
wish, fill it with complaints. If you
wish, adorn it with good deeds. When
the final page is turned, it will only
be seen how many lives you filled with
light. Only the one who lived for
others truly lived a meaningful life.
Shri Krishna says time is like sand
that slips away faster the tighter you
clench it in your fist. People say they
don't have time, while the truth is
that everyone has the same amount. The
only difference is that some cultivate
it, while others waste it. A person who
spends the first hour of the morning in
laziness spends the whole day paying
the debt of that hour. So, when your
eyes open, do not lie in bed making
excuses. Get up, wash your face, and
give your day a small resolution. It is
not necessary for the resolution to be
big. It just needs to be sincere. A
person who keeps a small promise to
themselves every day slowly becomes
worthy of their own trust. And the day
you become worthy of your own trust, no
storm in the world will be able to
shake you. One who curses time always
lags behind, and one who respects time
moves ahead of it. Shri Krishna says
habits are like a mill that keeps
grinding silently, and you don't even
realize when your life turned from
grain into flour. A bad habit initially
arrives like a guest. Then it becomes a
friend, and eventually, it turns into
the owner and takes over the house.
That is why you must recognize the
guest at the doorstep itself. Anything
that seems to give you pleasure today,
but will steal your sleep, health, or
honor tomorrow, say goodbye to it today
. Forming a good habit is definitely
difficult, but its fruit is very sweet.
The first few days will feel like you
are fighting against yourself. Let it
happen. He who has conquered himself,
no one in the world can defeat him.
Every major change is born from a small
repetition. Just as a pitcher is not
filled drop by drop, but the ocean of
the mind is, character is built through
small daily practices. And character is
the only capital that never goes
bankrupt. Shri Krishna says discipline
is not a shackle, it is the string of a
kite. As long as the string is in hand,
the kite touches the sky, and the
moment the string breaks, that same
kite falls to the ground like a severed
leaf. Those who say they don't want to
be bound by any rules do not know that
even a river reaches the ocean only by
being bound within its banks. If the
banks break, that same river becomes a
flood and devastates villages.
Discipline means doing what is
necessary on time, whether you feel
like it or not. Everyone knows how to
work when the mind is willing. The true
mark of a person is one who takes a
step even without the mind's consent.
When Arjuna had put down his bow, it
was not his mind but his duty that
picked it up. Within you too, there is
a chariot whose reins are in your own
hands. No matter how fast the horses
are, the charioteer decides the
direction. Shri Krishna says the body
is a chariot, and maintaining it is
your primary duty. A person who loses
their health in earning wealth
throughout their life. In old age, they
set out to buy health with that same
wealth and return empty-handed. Fresh
morning air, timely meals, sufficient
sleep, and a little sweat. These four
things are greater than any medicine in
a hospital. People sell their sleep to
save money and then spend money to get
sleep. What a strange bargain this is.
Your body is your temple. Whatever you
put into it, put it in thoughtfully.
Food that makes the stomach heavy and
the mind sluggish is not nutrition, it
is a burden. And the person who listens
to their body, their body supports them
until old age. So do not say that there
is still a long life ahead. The care
taken in youth is the greatest pension
for old age. Shri Krishna says failure
is not an enemy; it is a harsh but
honest teacher. It does not flatter you
, but it tells you the truth that no
sycophant in the world will tell you. A
person who succeeds on the first
attempt often does not know how success
was achieved, and that is why they
crumble when difficulty arrives. But
one who has learned to get up 100 times
after falling 100 times remembers the
entire map of their victory. Only when
gold is rubbed against a touchstone
does its true luster emerge. So,
whenever you face defeat, do not sit
holding your head, but ask: what lesson
is hidden here for me? Every defeat
carries within it the seed of a future
victory. One just needs the eyes to
recognize it. And remember, no one
becomes small by falling. One becomes
small by staying down after falling.
Shri Krishna says silence is a language
that needs no words to be understood.
When the mind is making too much noise,
becoming silent is the greatest
solution. Those who keep speaking all
the time lose the joy of listening, and
those who learn to listen understand
half the matter even before speaking.
Look at the flute; it is hollow from
within. That is why melodies emerge
from it. Those who are filled from
within with their ego, complaints, and
haste. How will music play in their
lives? Therefore, take out a few
moments every day for silence. In those
moments, you will hear the voices of
your own mind that you had suppressed
in the hustle and bustle of the day.
The greatest power of silence is that
it leads you not to respond, but to
understand, and one who understands
never needs to respond. Shri Krishna
says self-confidence is not a gift
received at birth; it is an earned
honor. When you complete a task, a
corner within you says, "Look, I can do
this." As these corners join together,
they form an entire fortress. A person
who considers themselves weak without
even trying writes their own defeat
with their own hands. Remember the day
when you sat on a bicycle for the first
time; you fell, your knees were scraped
. But that same evening, you had
balanced yourself on two wheels. Back
then, no one gave you a lecture. You
simply did not give up trying. That
same child is still alive within you
today. Wake them up. Tell them the
world is vast, but your steps can be
even bigger than it. When you learn to
believe in yourself, the world will
also have to believe in you. Lord
Krishna says service is a devotion that
requires no mantras and no temples.
When you hold an elderly person's hand
and help them cross the street. When
you show the way to someone who is lost
. When you sit by a sick person's
bedside and stroke their forehead, you
participate in the greatest of rituals.
One who serves never keeps track of how
much they have done. They simply feel
grateful for the opportunity to be of
use to someone. Those who serve and
then boast about it make their service
worthless the very same moment. True
service is always secret. Like a river
flowing underground, which remains
unseen but keeps the entire forest lush
. And those who taste the joy of
service once, find every other
sweetness in the world bland. Lord
Krishna says Sudama did not have a
golden platter. He just had a handful
of rice. Yet, I was satisfied after
eating it. Because in that rice, there
was his pure and selfless love. In
friendship, the value lies not in the
gift, but in the sentiment. A friend
who embraces you in your poverty and
does not forget you in your prosperity
is not just a friend, but the greatest
blessing of your life. And remember, I
did not give Sudama anything because he
asked for it. I gave him everything
even without him asking. True love
recognizes not those who ask, but those
who care in silence. Therefore, never
consider your friends small, and if you
become someone's Sudama, never be
ashamed of your poverty. Anything that
is sold in the world can have a price
set for it. But friendship is among
those rare few things that have no
price. Lord Krishna says greed is a
thirst that remains unquenched even
after drinking an ocean. Those who have
a thousand want ten thousand. Those who
have ten thousand want a hundred
thousand. And in this race, they forget
that what they were running after was
already in their bag. A greedy person
is like a fish that sees the shine of
the bait but misses the hook.
Contentment does not mean you stop
dreaming. It means you learn to value
what you have already received. Those
who are not happy with what they have
today will not be happy with what they
get tomorrow. Because happiness lies
not in things, but in the way one
perceives them. Therefore, keep a firm
rein on your desires. Desires are like
horses. If they remain under control,
they take you to your destination. If
they become uncontrollable, they cast
you into a ditch. Lord Krishna says
sleep is God's lap, in which a weary
person forgets everything and is reborn
. A person who sleeps peacefully at
night has surely done something good
during the day. And the one who keeps
tossing and turning has an unresolved
regret sitting at their bedside.
Therefore, account for your day before
going to sleep. If you spoke harshly to
someone, ask for forgiveness in your
heart. If you hurt someone's feelings,
promise to make it up to them in the
morning. And say thank you for
everything that went well. Then lay
your head on the pillow and leave
everything else to me. He who sleeps
after unburdening his mind has a
morning as fresh as a child's smile.
Sleep is not a luxury; it is the cure
for your soul. Shri Krishna says that
speaking is an art, and staying silent
is an even greater art. Words are like
arrows. Once released, they do not
return. So, when you speak, do it as if
you are placing a plate of flowers
before someone. It is necessary to
speak the truth, but the way of
speaking a bitter truth should be sweet
. The truth that pricks like a thorn
often never reaches the listener's
heart. And the truth that is wrapped in
love can melt even stone. Do not speak
ill of anyone behind their back.
Because the one who speaks ill of
others before you today will speak ill
of you before others tomorrow. Look
into the eyes of the person you are
talking to. Do not interrupt them, and
do not start preparing your answer
until they have finished speaking. The
one who listens is the true speaker.
Shri Krishna says faith is not a wall
against which one rests their head and
forgets their responsibility. It is the
bridge that stands between effort and
result. When a farmer plows the field,
he is the one who sows the seeds. But
he has no control over the raindrops
falling from the sky. This trust is
what is called faith. The person who
accepts that I will do my work with
complete honesty and leave the rest in
the hands of the Almighty. Restlessness
never takes root in their mind.
Restlessness arises when we want to
hold the result in our own fist. Faith
does not mean closing your eyes; it
means realizing that my understanding
has a limit, and beyond that limit,
there is someone who sees everything.
When your mind wavers, pause for a
moment and say, "Lord, I have done my
part.""Now, please show me the way
forward." Believe me, there is such
power in that one sentence that
mountain-like worries become as light
as cotton wool. Lord Krishna says a
daughter is the light of the home that
silently illuminates the entire
courtyard. In a home where a daughter
laughs, even the walls smile. He who
considers a daughter a burden does not
know that she carries the honor of two
families on her shoulders. Educate her.
Teach her to speak up. Make her so
strong that she does not depend on
anyone’s support. And teach sons too
that respecting women is not their
weakness, but their greatest strength.
A society where there is fear in a
woman’s eyes, no matter how much it
progresses, remains hollow from within.
I had heard Draupadi’s cry. Because
when a woman seeks justice with a true
heart, even the heavens have to bow
down. Therefore, give every daughter
the respect she deserves. And tell
every daughter that you are second to
none. Your dreams are as vast as the
sky. Lord Krishna says the true meaning
of education is not just memorizing
books, but learning to read life. A
person who, despite having a pile of
degrees, has not learned to speak to
their parents with respect, their
education is incomplete. Education
teaches you how to earn a living. But
values make you a human being.
Knowledge is the wealth that increases
by sharing and decreases by hiding. He
who passed his knowledge to others, his
knowledge became immortal. Therefore,
never lose the habit of being a student
. Whether you turn 50 or 80. If the
hunger for learning is alive within you
, you are young. And the day you feel
there is nothing left to learn, that is
the day your old age begins. Curiosity
is the lamp that shows the way in the
dark rooms of ignorance. Lord Krishna
says old age is not a curse, it is that
phase of life where a person needs the
most respect and time. The hands that
taught you to walk, today when they
tremble, it is your duty to hold them.
Abandoning elderly parents in an
old-age home is not just leaving them,
but hanging your own portrait for the
next generation to follow. Because your
children will learn what they see you
doing. The tree that keeps its dry
leaves in its shade is the one that
gets laden with flowers in the next
spring. Sit with the elderly. Listen to
their stories. Taste the flavor of
their experiences. Every wrinkle of
theirs is a whole book that is not
found in any university. And when they
repeat old stories, do not get annoyed,
because they are not sharing their
memories, but their loneliness. A
little bit of time and a little bit of
love, that is all they need. Shri
Krishna says that today's human sits
before a glowing screen, connected to
the whole world. Yet, they remain a
stranger in their own home. You spend
hours watching glimpses of others '
lives and forget that those glimpses
only show what is worth showing. Don't
assume someone is truly happy just by
seeing a smile in a picture. And don't
think you have been left behind just by
looking at your own simple life. This
marketplace of comparison is the
biggest thief of your peace. Put the
phone away sometimes and look at the
person sitting in front of you. The
message in their eyes will not be found
on any screen. In the time you waste on
meaningless scrolling, you could have
made someone weeping laugh. You could
have reconnected with a forgotten
relationship. Technology is a good
servant. But when it becomes the master
, human empathy dies first. Shri
Krishna says a neighbor is a
relationship that, despite not being
blood, is the first to come to your aid
. When someone falls suddenly ill at
night, by the time the news reaches
distant relatives, it is too late. But
a neighbor's knock arrives in an
instant. Therefore, maintain a good
relationship with your neighbor.
Participate in their joy. Offer your
shoulder in their sorrow and do not
build walls over trivial matters. Where
people live in harmony, no difficulty
is too great. I did not lift Mount
Govardhan alone. All the cowherds had
placed their sticks to support it. A
single hand cannot lift a mountain. But
when hundreds of hands come together,
even a mountain becomes an umbrella.
This is the true strength of society.
So, whenever you feel the burden is too
heavy, do not hesitate to call others
to lend their support, and when someone
calls you, arrive first with your help.
Shri Krishna says renunciation does not
mean leaving everything and going to
the forest. Renunciation means letting
go of the things within you that cause
pain to you and others. Whether it is
your anger, your ego, or your
stubbornness. A mother who feeds the
last piece of bread from her plate to
her child is the most beautiful example
of sacrifice. And a brother who gives
up his share of land to embrace his
brother earns a wealth far greater than
that land. Brothers fighting brothers
over property is the greatest defeat.
The entire story of the Mahabharata is
proof of this. Where one stubborn act
swallowed an entire dynasty. Five
villages were all that were asked for.
Not even a needle's point worth of land
was given, and in the end, the entire
kingdom turned to ash. Therefore,
whenever you clash with your own over
something, think: is this thing bigger
than them? The answer will always be
the same. Shri Krishna says that a
promise is an oath a person takes
before their own soul. Once you have
given your word, you must keep it like
a line carved in stone. A person who
breaks promises at every turn gradually
loses the value of their own word. And
one whose word has no value, has no
value themselves. So, if you make a
promise, think carefully, and once made
, fulfill it no matter what happens. It
is better to flatly refuse what you
cannot fulfill than to make a hundred
false promises. In today’s world,
people say that telling a little lie
gets the job done. It might get the job
done, but it ruins the character of the
one doing it. And a person whose
character is ruined, even with all the
world's comforts, is left with nothing.
The speech of one who speaks the truth
has a unique edge that needs no volume.
Shri Krishna says that Dharma does not
mean a method of worship, but the
courage to choose right between right
and wrong. When Arjuna stood before his
own teachers and his own family, his
hand trembled because he felt that
standing against his own was a sin.
Then I explained to him that supporting
injustice out of attachment to one's
own is the greatest sin. Life often
brings a turning point when you have to
stand against the wrongdoings of a
loved one. At that time, your heart
will weep, but choosing duty is what
Dharma is. A person who remains silent
upon seeing injustice becomes an equal
partner in that injustice. Therefore,
do not be afraid to speak in favor of
the truth. You may end up standing
alone. But the one who is with the
truth has the entire universe standing
with them. Shri Krishna says compassion
is the virtue that turns a
stone-hearted person into a human. A
heart that does not stir upon seeing
the suffering of others is not a heart,
but a beating stone. Do not look away
upon seeing that hungry child sitting
by the roadside. Because it is possible
that a blessing for you is hidden in
that child’s eyes. Have compassion
for animals, trees, rivers, and every
living being. One who keeps water in
the courtyard for a bird will never
face thirst in their own home. And
remember, compassion does not just mean
giving money or listening. Sometimes,
it means seating someone with respect.
Sometimes, it means not taking
someone's mistake to heart. These are
also forms of kindness. A kind person
may have little, but what they possess
is more valuable than a king's treasury
because it is stored in people's hearts
. Lord Krishna says, in my childhood, I
used to steal butter. But there was no
bad intention in that theft. It was
merely a mischief born of love. The
greatest virtue of children is their
pure mind. They fight today and start
playing together again tomorrow because
they hold no grudges in their hearts.
As we grow up, this is the first thing
we lose. We carry the knots of old
grievances in our hearts and then
complain that life has become heavy. If
you want to feel light again, remember
the child who takes not a moment to
forgive someone. Keep the child within
you alive. Let them laugh. Let them
play. Let them be amazed by the
smallest of things. The person who
preserves their inner innocence remains
young even in old age. Lord Krishna
says, honesty is the wealth that
thieves cannot steal and time cannot
diminish. The merchant who does not
cheat on the scales has customers
returning for generations. The servant
who works just as hard behind the
master's back as in front of them
becomes a master themselves one day.
Today people run after shortcuts, but
shortcuts often lead to a street that
ends in a wall. The straight path may
seem long, but it is the one that leads
to the destination. Therefore, do not
let there be any flaws in your work.
Whether someone is watching or not. Do
your work as if God himself is watching
. Because he truly is watching. The
person who is honest even when alone is
the truly honest one. It is easy to act
like a saint in front of a crowd. But
remaining a saint in solitude is the
true penance. Lord Krishna says a
family is a tree whose roots lie in the
blessings of ancestors and whose
branches spread into the dreams of
future generations. In the family where
everyone eats together from the same
plate. Prosperity arrives there on its
own. Where everyone takes their own
separate path and stops asking about
each other's well-being. There, houses
may grow larger, but homes become
smaller. Therefore, sit with everyone
once a week. Talk about the old days.
Let the children listen to the stories
of their grandparents. These are the
moments that later become the most
precious memories. In a family, no one
is small or big. Everyone is a
complement to one another. A single
finger cannot lift anything, but when
five fingers join, they form a fist,
and that fist holds great power. Shri
Krishna says that change is the most
absolute law of this universe. The leaf
that is green today will turn yellow
tomorrow, and the day after, it will
merge with the soil to become
fertilizer for a new tree. A person who
fears change stands on the very bank
that the river is slowly eroding away.
Learn to move with the times. Uphold
the traditions that bring people
together. But have the courage to
change any custom that causes harm to
others. Change is not a sign of
weakness, but a sign of being alive. If
water remains stagnant in one place, it
begins to rot, but if it keeps flowing,
it is called the Ganga. Therefore, when
a new turn comes in life, do not be
afraid. That very turn might lead you
to the place you always wanted to reach
. It is just that the path was
different from what you thought. Shri
Krishna says that when two paths lie
before you and your mind cannot decide,
first ask your inner voice which of
these paths will give you a peaceful
night's sleep. Dilemma arises when we
fear the consequences of a decision.
Not the decision itself. But remember,
not taking a decision is also a
decision, and often, that is the worst
decision of all. A person who keeps
counting the dust on every path can
never walk on any path at all. So,
think a little, and seek advice from
your elders. Then listen to your heart
and take the step forward. If the path
turns out to be wrong, there is no
shame in turning back. The one who
returns and takes the right direction
is far ahead of the one who stubbornly
keeps walking on the wrong path. It is
better to turn back from the middle of
the way than to reach a wrong
destination. Shri Krishna says a true
leader is not the one who stands in
front and gives orders, but the one who
stays at the very back to support the
exhausted. I did not pick up a weapon
at Kurukshetra. Yet, I became the
charioteer of the entire war. Because
leadership means showing the right
direction, not showing power. A leader
who takes the credit for his team's
work for himself gradually becomes
alone. And the one who gives credit for
every success to his team, people are
ready to lay down their lives for him.
The first condition of leadership is
that you must do what you expect others
to do. The one who sits in laziness and
preaches hard work to others, his words
vanish into thin air. If you want
people to listen to you, then first
give weight to your words through your
own actions. Lord Krishna says that one
who walks alone may walk fast, but one
who walks together walks far. When you
take on a big task, do not harbor the
arrogance of doing everything alone.
Every person possesses some quality
that you do not have. Bring them along
with you. Listen to what they have to
say. Give them respect. Just as a
chariot needs horses, wheels, reins,
and a charioteer, the effort of
different people joins together to
achieve every great goal. He who values
even the smallest person in the team
never loses. Because everyone feels
that this victory is theirs too. And
the work in which everyone feels a
sense of belonging does not remain a
burden; it becomes a celebration. Lord
Krishna says simplicity is the jewel
that shines brighter than the most
expensive diamonds. A person who walks
with self-respect even in simple
clothes. Even those in high palaces bow
their heads before them. Showing off is
a burden that a person places on their
own shoulders and then complains of
being tired. People will not respect
you for your clothes, but for your
behavior. Therefore, keep only what is
necessary and consider the rest to be a
share for others. The happiness I found
in Sudama's hut is not found in any
golden palace. Whoever learns to be
happy with less, no one can make them
poor. And whoever remains dissatisfied
even after getting much, no one can
make them rich. Simple living and high
thinking is the simple formula for a
successful life. Lord Krishna says
focus is the power that brings a
scattered mind to a single point. Just
as sunlight passing through a lens
gathers at a point and burns paper.
Likewise, when your mind stays fixed on
one task, even the impossible becomes
possible. Today's human is running in
10 directions at once. That is why they
never reach anywhere. When you read,
just read. When you eat, just eat. When
you talk to someone, be fully present
with them. Arjuna saw nothing but the
bird's eye, and that is why his arrow
hit the target. You should also have a
goal in life on which your eyes remain
fixed. One whose eyes wander at every
shiny object. Ends up with nothing in
their hands. Lord Krishna says sorrow
is a person's greatest teacher. Even if
its fee is very high. In happiness, a
person sleeps, and in sorrow, they wake
up. When everything is going well, we
neither look within ourselves nor
remember God. But when we get hurt, we
stop and think about who we are and
what we want. So, do not consider
sorrow a curse. Consider it a strict
teacher who is shaping you. Even a
diamond shines only when it is polished
. Those who have seen much sorrow in
life have a unique compassion for
others because they know what it feels
like to break. Make your sorrow your
strength, and when you rise yourself,
hold someone else's hand. Shri Krishna
says there is no greater teacher than
nature. Learn from the tree how to
remain humble even after bearing fruit.
Learn from the river how to find a way
even amidst obstacles. Learn from the
mountain how to remain steadfast. And
learn from the earth how to remain
silent even while bearing everyone's
burden. A person who loves nature like
a mother is never troubled by
loneliness. Because every morning the
chirping of birds wakes them, and every
evening the setting sun blesses them.
Today, man has cut trees, polluted
rivers, and poisoned the air, and now
complains that it is hard to breathe.
Saving the earth is not a favor. It is
saving your own life. Plant a tree,
water a plant, and see how much peace
descends within you. Shri Krishna says
humility is a tree whose branches bend
the more they are laden with fruit. The
person who remains grounded even after
reaching great heights is truly
elevated. Arrogance is a color that
fades first in the eyes of others and
then in one's own. When you talk to
someone, do not let them feel that you
are greater than them. The day you feel
that you know the most, ask a child a
question that day. Perhaps you will
realize your own limits. Ravana was
wise and powerful, but his ego brought
him to a point where everything turned
to dust. Great is he who forgets his
own status and meets his juniors just
as he meets his equals. Shri Krishna
says the essence of Karma Yoga is that
you do your work with full devotion and
do not burn your present worrying about
its fruits. When you work worrying
about the results, your mind gets
divided into two places. One in the
work and the other in the fear of the
future, and because of this, the work
remains incomplete. But when you
immerse your whole mind in the work,
the work itself becomes a spiritual
practice. You have the right only to
your duty. Not to the outcome. It
sounds difficult to hear. But the
greatest freedom is hidden within it.
One who is freed from the chains of
results does not break in defeat, nor
does he get carried away in victory.
His mind remains as calm as a lake in
which even a pebble cannot raise a
ripple. Shri Krishna says criticism is
a fire that, even if lit in another's
house, brings smoke into one's own eyes
. The person who spends the day
counting others' flaws has no time left
to fix his own, and do not be angry
with those who criticize you, for they
are washing away your sins without you
even asking. Your only response to
those who criticize you should be your
work. Do not lend an ear to rumors, and
do not form an opinion about anyone
until you have seen it with your own
eyes. How many relationships have been
broken by a mere hearsay, and how many
homes have been ruined by someone's
lies. Therefore, when someone comes to
you with gossip about another,
understand that tomorrow they will take
your gossip to someone else. Shri
Krishna says competition is good as
long as it makes you better, but when
it makes you bitter, it is poison. Do
not consider someone else's victory as
your defeat. The world is big enough
that there is room for everyone. Just
as there is a place for every star in
the sky. Yet, no star pushes another
out of the way. One who is truly
capable does not need to pull anyone
down. His own work elevates him.
Respect your competitor too, because
they tell you how much hard work you
need to put in. Often, our best
teachers are the very ones we consider
our enemies. He who can learn even from
his enemy cannot be defeated by anyone
in the world. Shri Krishna says
welcoming a guest is India's oldest
tradition, and it is not a show, but a
sentiment. When someone comes to your
door, serve them whatever you have with
love. Even dry bread served with love
tastes sweeter than a feast, and even a
feast served with contempt becomes
bitter. At Vidur's house, I ate banana
peels because he served them with
devotion. The taste of devotion is the
highest of all. Therefore, never think
that you have nothing significant to
offer. Your smiling face, your sweet
words, and a place to sit—these three
things are in every home and are enough
to win any guest's heart. Shri Krishna
says festivals are not just for
lighting lamps or distributing sweets.
They are meant so that a person can
pause and refresh their relationships.
When you sit together with everyone
during a festival, old bitterness
begins to fade away on its own.
Therefore, do not observe every
festival just as a ritual. Make it an
opportunity to connect with your loved
ones. Call someone who is upset with
you. Deliver sweets to the home of
someone in need. Sit for a while with
an elderly person who is alone. A
celebration in which the hungry do not
get food and the sad do not find a
smile is incomplete. A real Diwali is
when, because of you, light returns to
a faded face. Shri Krishna says that
the mind is restless like a monkey.
When it catches one branch, it becomes
restless to jump to another. If you try
to restrain it forcefully, it will jump
even more. But if you reason with it
lovingly, it will gradually become your
best friend. The senses are like horses
that run toward every patch of green
grass. The eyes want to see only what
shines. The tongue wants to taste only
what is sweet, and the ears want to
hear only praise. The person who keeps
the reins of these horses in their
hands leads the chariot of life to the
right destination. Self-control does
not mean killing your desires. It means
placing them at the right time and in
the right place. Food that is eaten on
time and in moderation is like nectar.
And if that same food is eaten without
limits, it becomes poison. Moderation
in everything is the mother of
happiness. Shri Krishna says that
crying is not a sign of weakness. Just
as clouds clear the sky by raining,
tears lighten the burden of the mind as
they flow. A man who holds back his
tears thinking about what people will
say, gradually turns into stone from
within. And no one knows how many
storms are hidden behind the smile of a
woman who silently endures her pain. So
, when your heart feels heavy, cry
openly in front of someone close to you
. And when someone cries in front of
you, do not be in a hurry to silence
them. Just sit beside them. Sometimes,
the greatest comfort is not in words,
but in the feeling of just being
together. One who learns to view the
tears of others with respect can never
have a heart of stone. Shri Krishna
says when the mind becomes very
depressed and you have no desire to do
anything, do not consider it your
weakness. It could also be an illness
for which treatment is possible. Just
as you go to a doctor when the body
falls ill, do not feel ashamed to talk
to a loved one or an expert when the
mind gets tired. Do not insist on
dealing with your sadness alone. A
burden that can break you if carried
alone, becomes lighter when shared
across many shoulders. Never think that
your absence won't matter to anyone.
Wherever you stand, there is someone
whose world is brightened by your
presence. So, when the darkness feels
too deep, hold someone’s hand and say
, "I need a little support today." Even
saying this is an act of courage. Shri
Krishna says love is not what is born
from the desire to possess. Love is
what blossoms in the joy of giving.
Radha never asked me for anything. Yet,
her name is taken before mine because
her love was not bound by any
expectations. Love that carries a sense
of ownership gradually becomes a
shackle, and love that holds freedom is
the highest form of love. Give the one
you love an open sky to fly. Not a cage
. If they are yours, they will return,
and if they don't, they were never
yours to begin with. Separation in love
can also be a kind of union if there is
no bitterness in the heart. Even after
going to Mathura, I never forgot Gokul,
and Radha waited for me for years
without a single complaint. Shri
Krishna says marriage is not a union of
two humans, but of two souls. When two
people vow to walk together, they do
not just become partners in happiness.
They become partners in sorrow as well.
The secret to a successful marriage is
not that there are no fights, but that
after a fight, one of them reaches out
first. Both should remember that they
are not opponents, but passengers in
the same boat. If even one lets go of
the oar, the boat will sink, and both
will drown equally. Handle each
other’s flaws as you handle your own,
and appreciate each other’s virtues
as you hope to be appreciated by the
world. A relationship in which words of
praise and gratitude stay alive never
grows old. Shri Krishna says youth is a
river with a very strong current; he
who gives it the right direction can
generate electricity from it. But for
one who lets it flow aimlessly, this
very current becomes a flood. To the
youth of today, I have this to say:
your strength is immense. Do not waste
it on pointless debates, intoxication,
or showing off. The energy you waste
staying up all night on useless things,
invest it into a dream. You have time,
you have health, you have enthusiasm,
and if these three things slip away
once, they never return. So, decide
today what you want to become and set
out on that path. He who sows the seeds
of hard work in his youth reaps a
harvest of peace in his old age. Lord
Krishna says, life is like a boat and
the mind is its rudder. If the rudder
is in your hands, you will find the
shore even in a storm. But if you leave
the rudder to the waves, even a calm
sea can drown you. Therefore, before
blaming circumstances, see in which
direction your mind is heading. There
are some wounds that are healed not by
medicine, but by time. And there are
some wounds that even time cannot heal.
One simply learns to live with them. Do
not consider yourself weak during such
times. The one who endures pain yet
does not inflict pain on others is the
truly strong person. The struggle
hidden behind their smile cannot be
written in any book. If someone has
done you wrong, do not waste your time
in the fire of revenge. Leave them to
their own karma. Nature's accounting is
very precise. There is neither any
delay there, nor any mistake. Whoever
is happy pulling others down today will
have to fall into the pit they dug
tomorrow. You just keep doing your part
well and leave the rest behind. Prayer
is not just the name of asking for
things. True prayer is one in which a
person says, "O Lord, thank you for
what you have given, and give me the
strength to handle what you will give
in the future." Whoever joins their
hands with this sentiment, the
restlessness within them automatically
calms down. Then they no longer worry
about what will happen tomorrow because
they know that the one who took care of
today will also take care of tomorrow.
Lord Krishna says addiction is that
sweet poison which first embraces you
like a friend and then chokes your
throat. The person who turns to
addiction thinking "just once" or "just
a little bit" sets foot on a slope
where stopping is no longer in their
control. Addiction does not make you
forget sorrow, it deepens it, and when
the effect wears off, the same sorrow
returns with double the intensity. If
you feel you are trapped in a bad habit
, do not be ashamed and do not fight
alone. Tell someone close to you and
seek help from an expert. Quitting an
addiction is difficult, but not
impossible. Anyone who finds the
courage even for one day to say, "Today
I will not drink." He is moving towards
winning the biggest battle of his life,
and the one who falls and rises again,
I am the first to embrace him. Shri
Krishna says that in business, your
name is your greatest capital. The one
who breaks a customer's trust once may
keep their shop running, but their
reputation dies. Do earn a profit, but
not so much that you start taking
advantage of someone's helplessness.
The merchant who treats a poor customer
with as much respect as a rich one may
have a small safe, but their bank of
blessings is never empty. Treat your
employees like family. The employer who
pays the worker's wages before their
sweat dries is favored by Goddess
Lakshmi herself. And remember, wealth
only stays when it is earned ethically.
Ill-gotten gains come like floodwaters,
and like floodwaters, they wash
everything away. Shri Krishna says
people ask whether hard work is greater
or destiny? I say that hard work is the
plow that it is your job to drive. And
destiny is the rain that is not in your
hands. If you don't plow, even the rain
will fall on barren land and return in
vain. And if the rain doesn't come even
after plowing, do not be sad, because
the land will be ready and the rain
will surely come one day. The person
who sits waiting for destiny never
achieves anything. And the one who
relies only on hard work, believing
everything is in their control, breaks
at the first stumble. Balance is the
right path. Work as if everything
depends on you. And accept the results
as if everything depends on God. Shri
Krishna says, opportunity is a guest
that passes by the door without
knocking. The one who stays alert
recognizes it, and the one who sleeps
in laziness only gets to hear the sound
of its footsteps. Opportunity does not
always come in a big form. Sometimes it
comes in the form of a small task.
Sometimes as the smile of a stranger,
and sometimes as a difficult situation.
The one who performs every small task
with full dedication is the one
prepared for a big opportunity.
Therefore, always keep yourself
prepared. Keep learning, keep meeting
people, and when it knocks at the door,
have the courage to get up and open it.
Also remember that many times, behind
the door that closes, another bigger
door is waiting for you. Shri Krishna
says, learn to listen to criticism
because the one who praises you makes
you happy. But the one who criticizes
you, improves you. Not every critic is
an enemy. Some of them are your
greatest well-wishers, who point out
your mistakes so that you can rise even
higher. Yes, not every criticism is
worth accepting. Some people speak only
to vent their bitterness. Identify them
and let their words blow away in the
wind. Keep the words that are useful to
you. Leave the rest behind. Just as a
swan can separate milk from water, a
listener must know how to distinguish
between what is useful and what is
useless. That is where wisdom lies.
Shri Krishna says that apologizing is
as difficult as it is powerful. When
you sincerely tell someone that you
made a mistake, that one sentence can
bring down walls built over years. A
person who hesitates to admit their
mistake is actually protecting their
ego, not the relationship. And ego is
the thing that leaves last and causes
the most damage. So, whenever you feel
that you have made a mistake, do not
delay. That is the best time to
apologize. When you first realize it.
Delaying makes the issue bigger, and
putting it off makes the wound deeper.
And when someone apologizes to you,
accept it with a big heart. It is your
duty to lift up the one who had the
courage to bow. Shri Krishna says,
never forget your birthplace. The soil
where you first learned to walk, the
courtyard where you heard your mother's
lullabies, that place always stays
alive within you. I left Gokul and went
to Dwarka. But in my flute, the waves
of the Yamuna still resonate today. So,
do not get lost in the dazzle of the
city and forget the scent of your
village soil. Return from time to time.
Sit under the old banyan tree. Meet old
friends and water your roots once again
. Those who remember their roots, no
matter how high they reach, their feet
always remain on the ground. And one
who loves their country, their love is
not just in the flag, but reflects in
their honesty, their duty, and their
character. Shri Krishna says,
disrespecting food is disrespecting God
. When you leave leftovers on your
plate, you insult the sweat of the
farmer who toiled in the sun to grow
that grain. Before eating, pause for a
moment to remember the earth, the
farmer, and the hands that filled your
plate. Take only as much as you can eat
. And if ever a hungry person comes to
your door, do not send them away
empty-handed. A home from which no
hungry person leaves unsatisfied will
never face a shortage of food. Respect
every single drop of water because it
is the foundation of life. Those who
waste water are inviting thirst upon
their own future. Lord Krishna says
this life is a journey and we are all
travelers. Some walk with us for a
little distance. Some for a long way,
and some leave us midway. Do not wait
for those who have left. And do not
forget to value those who are with you.
The biggest mistake in this journey is
that we keep watching those who leave
and forget to look at those walking by
our side. When you get tired, stop and
catch your breath, but do not settle
there. There is a difference between
resting and stagnating. Resting is
preparation for the next step, while
stagnation is giving up. Those who do
not lose sight of their goal even when
tired, the paths themselves begin to
make way for them. I have only one
lesson: keep your heart pure. Keep your
intentions high and your feet on the
ground. If your heart is pure, your
relationships will last. If your
intentions are high, you will reach
your destination, and if your feet are
on the ground, no height will be able
to make you fall. When the time comes
to depart from this world, let there be
no burden in your mind. Let there be no
bitterness for anyone, and when you go
before God, may your head be held high
with pride rather than bowed down. This
is the greatest earning of life and
this is every person's true destination
. Lord Krishna says the greatest enemy
of knowledge is ego, because one who
assumes he knows everything leaves no
room within to learn. A full vessel
cannot hold anything else, and it is
the empty vessel that makes the most
noise. One who is truly great learns
something even from the humblest of
people. How strange it is that we can
easily see the straw in others 'eyes,
but we fail to see the log in our own.
If every person looked in the mirror
once a day, half of all conflicts would
end automatically. A lifetime is spent
trying to change others, but changing
oneself takes only a single decision.
The thing that poisons relationships
the most is comparison. When you
compare your home to others', your
children to neighbors ', or your
earnings to someone else's, you lose
the joy of what you already have. Every
person’s journey is different. Every
flower has its own time to bloom. If a
jasmine flower starts crying by looking
at a rose, it will lose its own
fragrance. For the person who does not
leave the side of truth even in trouble
, God himself makes a way. No matter
how tall the building of a lie may be,
its foundation is bound to shake one
day. And the hut of truth, even if
small, stands firm even in a storm. So,
do not use lies to win, because a
victory gained by defeating your own
conscience is truly the biggest defeat.
Shri Krishna says that a person who has
patience holds the key to unlock every
door. A step taken in haste often leads
us into the very pit we were running to
avoid. When you see no path, pause for
a moment. Pausing is not losing.
Sometimes, that is the most sensible
step to take. Only when the pond's
water is still, can the reflection of
the sky be seen clearly. People who get
troubled by every little thing forget
that trouble also comes like a guest
and leaves. It is our own mistake to
stop the guest at the door and make
them the master of the house. Let it
come, listen to what it has come to
teach you. Then bid it farewell. Give
time to your inner voice. In the hustle
and bustle of the day, carve out a few
moments just to sit with yourself. No
phone, no noise, no comparing with
anyone. In that silence, you will find
answers that you wouldn't get even
after asking thousands of people.
